messages:
maya: FYI — alex reported a Tool Call 400 when the tool_args include an embedded null and Windows-style backslashes. Customer says it worked earlier.
liam: can you paste the exact request body and the error text? quick repro would help.
alex: here's the payload we send from our client (JS):
```json
{
  "tool_name": "file_inspector",
  "tool_args": "{\"path\":\"C:\\Users\\alex\\file.txt\",\"note\":\"scan\\u0000end\"}"
}
```
Error returned: `400 Bad Request: invalid tool args JSON - unexpected control char at offset 56`
We think the `\\u0000` is making it fail when the server parses tool_args.
support-bot: :ticket: Ticket #INF-7423 created and linked to this thread.
maya: sounds like tool_args is a JSON-encoded string (double-encoded) and your client includes `\\u0000` which our parser ends up decoding into a literal null byte. some parsers choke on embedded NULs.
liam: can you share the curl repro (exact raw body) so I can test locally? I want to see whether our parser unescapes twice.
alex: sure — this is the curl we used (bash):
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/call_tool \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"tool_name":"file_inspector","tool_args":"{\"path\":\"C:\\Users\\alex\\file.txt\",\"note\":\"scan\\u0000end\"}"}'
```
This originates from our app code which JSON.stringify()s the inner args because the client lib expected a string.
ingrid: reproducing now. quick note: node's JSON.parse will turn `\\u0000` into a codepoint 0 in the JS string. if the platform then writes that into a buffer and our low-level JSON lexer sees a NUL it can break.
I see a failure in our lib: `json_lexer.c: parse_string(): unexpected '\0' in string` on parse.
liam: ok confirmed. gist: client sends tool_args as a string containing escaped JSON. our call handling does one json_decode on the body which produces a JS string for tool_args (with `\u0000` escape decoded -> actual NUL). then we attempt to parse that string again as JSON with our C-based parser which disallows NULs inside strings. double-unescape causes the real NUL to appear.
maya: proposed fixes: (1) short-term mitigation: reject requests where `tool_args` is a string with control chars and return an informative 400 instructing to pass an object; (2) medium-term: harden parser to safely reject/escape control chars instead of crashing; (3) long-term: update SDK docs and client libs to send tool_args as a JSON object rather than a JSON-encoded string.
liam: I can ship a small patch to detection logic in ~eng-runtime: return 400 with `error: "tool_args must be a JSON object, not an escaped JSON string containing control characters"`. patch snippet:
```c
// pseudo
if (is_string(tool_args_raw)) {
  if (contains_control_chars(tool_args_raw)) {
    return bad_request("tool_args must be a JSON object (no control chars)");
  }
  // attempt to parse but with safe check
}
```
I'll open PR and add a unit test for `\u0000` and `\u0001`.
maya: for support response to customer let's propose a playbook message. alex we can paste this and close the loop.
Suggested reply:
> Thanks — we found the root cause: your client is sending `tool_args` as a string that contains an embedded null (decoded from `\\u0000`) and our parser rejects NULs for safety. Workarounds: send `tool_args` as a JSON object (not a string) or remove control characters before sending. We're also adding a clearer 400 response to help detect this.
alex: Thanks, trying change now. I'll update our client to send the object directly:
```js
// instead of 
// tool_args: JSON.stringify({path: 'C:\\Users\\alex\\file.txt', note: 'scan\\u0000end'})
// send: 
{ tool_name: 'file_inspector', tool_args: { path: 'C:\\Users\\alex\\file.txt', note: 'scan\\u0000end' } }
```
Note: we still need to preserve note containing null for our internal parsing, but we can escape it differently.
ingrid: temporary mitigations rolled: added a gateway check to reject NUL-containing strings and return structured message. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/patches/inf-7423 (added test vectors). :white_check_mark:
liam: PR created and linked to ticket, adding a watch for any other control-char issues. also adding logging to capture `tool_args` type for a week to find similar patterns.
maya: assigning follow-up to eng-runtime for hardening. support will coordinate with alex for full validation.
alex: confirmed — after changing to send object, our calls succeed. thanks for the quick turnaround! :tada:
